claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy has a fine, dual-phase lamellar microstructure in the as-cast state.
The as-cast lamellar microstructure is prone to microcracking under tensile loading.
Single-pass sub-solidus friction stir processing will refine the alloy's lamellae.
Single-pass sub-solidus friction stir processing will disrupt crack-prone colony boundaries.
Friction stir processing will cause shear-induced partial breakup of the lamellae.
Dynamic recrystallization during friction stir processing will contribute to microstructural refinement.
The friction stir tool will mechanically mix the lamellar colonies.
Friction stir processing will disperse boundary defects and refine grains.
Reducing crack-prone intercolony interfaces will impede microcrack initiation.
The refined microstructure will increase strength through dislocation and grain-boundary strengthening.
The refined microstructure will increase ductility by promoting more uniform plastic flow.
Processed samples will develop fewer early cracks at colony boundaries than the as-cast baseline.
Processed samples will have greater room-temperature uniform elongation than the as-cast baseline.
Processed samples will maintain or slightly increase strength relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy has high room-temperature strength.
The as-cast baseline has limited room-temperature tensile ductility.
Keeping the process below the eutectic melting point will avoid partial melting.
Sufficient tool pressure is required to prevent void formation during processing.
Excessive tool speed or multiple passes may overheat the alloy or cause localized damage.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows strength merely to be retained, but the falsification rule can be read as falsifying the hypothesis whenever tensile strength shows no improvement. Thus, a result with unchanged strength and improved elongation would satisfy the stated prediction while potentially meeting the stated falsification criterion.
